features.text: Patient reports left arm pain with onset about two weeks ago, starting around 2:00 AM with severe pain.
Patient applied ice to the arm, which eased the pain.
Patient sat on the side of the bed and held the arm down to help circulation, but it did not help.
The pain subsided around 4-5 AM and did not recur during the night.
The pain recurred over several nights, prompting the patient to see a doctor.
The patient was diagnosed with a pinched nerve by a previous doctor.
The pain radiates from the neck down the arm.
The patient experiences intermittent pain, with symptoms worsening at night and affecting the following day.
The patient has a history of injuring the finger, which now has limited function.
The patient was prescribed numbing medicine, a neck pill, and gabapentin for the condition.
The patient is a VA patient and is 1% disabled due to leg issues from the knees down to the feet.
The patient has neuropathy, as confirmed by the patient.
The patient feels a slight strain in the neck when tilting the head.
The patient can grip with both hands, though the left arm is affected.
The patient does not take blood thinners, but is on Eliquis.
The patient's neck has not been bothering them for the last couple of nights.
The patient has been experiencing symptoms for the last week.
The patient prefers to proceed with the work-up and epidural.
The patient is scheduled for an MRI today.
